entry.title: Testnet 5 launch
entry.summary:
Mining of the testnet 5 genesis block is scheduled to take place at the end of the week, in coordination with the next mainnet retarget event at block 975,744. For those interested in contributing hashrate to the bootstrapping process of testnet5, comprehensive documentation on the procedure can be found [here](https://gist.github.com/ajtowns/ebb148819c6028387271e6f0dce5e1da). Additionally, a 0%-fee solo-mining pool is available to facilitate participation, and details for accessing this resource are provided [here](https://lapis.erisian.com.au/chain.html). Tests will continue at lower difficulty throughout the week until just before block 975,744 is mined.
Several modifications have been introduced to the genesis block structure, which are detailed in [this pull request](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2347). These changes aim to simplify pooled mining of the genesis block by providing extranonce space and explicitly allowing nVersion rolling. The modifications also bring the block format closer to prior genesis blocks by including the textual commitment in the pszTimestamp field instead of the output field, and by utilizing an unspendable OP_RETURN for the output, as opposed to a potentially post-quantum spendable x-point.
When initializing a new blockchain, inconsistencies in encoding the BIP 34 block height often cause issues. Bitcoin Core requires that blocks 1 to 16 use OP_1 to OP_16 in the coinbase, whereas much mining software anticipates a one-byte push, specifically using codes from 0x0101 to 0x0110. This discrepancy may lead to unexpected behavior at low block heights during chain bootstrapping. Further information and discussion regarding these nuances can be found in [this reference](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2342) and [this pull request](https://github.com/bitaxeorg/ESP-Miner/pull/2089).
